# Beak CSS

> Beak CSS is a classless, pure-CSS fork of Pico CSS v2.1.1. It styles plain
> semantic HTML with no classes, no SASS and no build step. Every token is a
> CSS custom property named `--beak-*`, and the whole framework ships inside
> `@layer beak`, so your own CSS always wins without specificity fights.

## Files

- [beak.min.css](https://beakcss.dev.ar/dist/beak.min.css): full-width build, the default. Use this in apps and dashboards.
- [beak.contained.min.css](https://beakcss.dev.ar/dist/beak.contained.min.css): same, plus a centered reading column for docs and blogs.
- [beak.css](https://beakcss.dev.ar/dist/beak.css) and [beak.contained.css](https://beakcss.dev.ar/dist/beak.contained.css): the same two builds, unminified.

## Usage

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/beakcss/dist/beak.min.css">
<!-- optional, exactly one theme, after the base: -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/beakcss/dist/themes/full/dracula.css">
```

- npm: `npm install beakcss`, then `import "beakcss"` (JS bundler) or link `node_modules/beakcss/dist/beak.min.css`.
- Light, dark and system mode come from the base: `data-theme="light|dark"` on `<html>`, or omit it to follow `prefers-color-scheme`.
- Load order: base → theme → your CSS. Never edit the shipped files; override the `--beak-*` variables instead.

## Example

A complete page — no classes, no wrappers, every component driven by markup:

```html
<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Beak</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/beakcss/dist/beak.min.css"></head><body>
<header><nav><ul><li><strong>Beak</strong></li></ul><ul><li><a href="#">Docs</a></li><li><a href="#">About</a></li></ul></nav></header>
<main>
<hgroup><h1>Title</h1><p>A subtitle in plain HTML.</p></hgroup>
<p>Paragraph with <a href="#">a link</a>, <strong>bold</strong>, <em>italic</em>, <code>inline code</code> and <mark>highlight</mark>.</p>
<blockquote>"Quote." <footer><cite>Source</cite></footer></blockquote>
<form>
<label>Name<input type="text" name="name" placeholder="Ada Lovelace"></label>
<label>Role<select name="role"><option>Developer</option><option>Designer</option></select></label>
<label><input type="checkbox" role="switch" checked> Notifications</label>
<label><input type="radio" name="plan" checked> Monthly</label>
<label><input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="42"></label>
<button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
<figure><table><thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Classless</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Beak</td><td>Yes</td></tr></tbody></table></figure>
<details><summary>More</summary><p>Collapsible content.</p></details>
</main>
<footer><small>Footer</small></footer>
</body></html>
```

## Themes

Two kinds, both loaded *after* the base stylesheet. Filenames are
`dist/themes/{name}.css` for tints, `dist/themes/full/{name}.css` for full
palettes.

1. **Tints** — Pico's 19 accent-only palettes; each swaps just the accent ramp
   and still follows the OS light/dark mode. Available: amber, blue, cyan, fuchsia, green, grey, indigo, jade, lime, orange, pink, pumpkin, purple, red, sand, slate, violet, yellow, zinc.
2. **Full palettes** — complete schemes with their own background, text,
   borders, code and form colors. A single flavour is *pinned* across light,
   system and dark, so a dark-only scheme never flips. Families with both
   flavours also ship a `{family}-auto.css` that follows
   `prefers-color-scheme` and `data-theme`.

Full palettes by family, `(l)` light and `(d)` dark:

- **Dracula**: `dracula` (d)
- **Nord**: `nord` (d), `nord-light` (l)
- **Catppuccin**: `catppuccin-latte` (l), `catppuccin-frappe` (d), `catppuccin-macchiato` (d), `catppuccin-mocha` (d)
- **Tokyo Night**: `tokyo-night` (d), `tokyo-night-storm` (d)
- **Gruvbox**: `gruvbox-dark` (d), `gruvbox-light` (l)
- **One Dark**: `one-dark` (d)
- **Monokai**: `monokai` (d)
- **Rosé Pine**: `rose-pine` (d), `rose-pine-moon` (d), `rose-pine-dawn` (l)
- **Solarized**: `solarized-light` (l), `solarized-dark` (d)
- **Everforest**: `everforest-dark` (d), `everforest-light` (l)
- **Kanagawa**: `kanagawa` (d)
- **Ayu**: `ayu-dark` (d), `ayu-mirage` (d), `ayu-light` (l)

Adaptive `{family}-auto` files, light/dark:

`nord-auto` = `nord-light`/`nord`; `catppuccin-auto` = `catppuccin-latte`/`catppuccin-mocha`; `gruvbox-auto` = `gruvbox-light`/`gruvbox-dark`; `rose-pine-auto` = `rose-pine-dawn`/`rose-pine`; `solarized-auto` = `solarized-light`/`solarized-dark`; `everforest-auto` = `everforest-light`/`everforest-dark`; `ayu-auto` = `ayu-light`/`ayu-dark`.

## Notes for LLMs

- There are no classes. Style the elements themselves: `header`, `main`, `nav`, `section`, `article`, `aside`, `footer`, `figure`, `table`, `form`, `fieldset`, `label`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `button`, `details`, `dialog`.
- Semantic attributes drive components: `role="switch"` on a checkbox renders a switch, `role="button"` styles a link as a button, `<details>` renders an accordion.
- Colors and measures are variables, not values to hardcode: `--beak-primary`, `--beak-background-color`, `--beak-color`, `--beak-spacing`, `--beak-border-radius`. Full list in the color-scheme blocks of `dist/beak.css`.
- Common aliases resolve out of the box: `--beak-accent` (= `--beak-primary`), `--beak-text-color` (= `--beak-color`), `--beak-bg` (= `--beak-background-color`), `--beak-link-color`, `--beak-success`, `--beak-danger`, `--beak-warning`, `--beak-info`, `--beak-font`, `--beak-radius`, `--beak-shadow`, `--beak-space`. Aliases are read-only: override the canonical name (e.g. `--beak-primary`, not `--beak-accent`).
- Themes are additive files inside the same `@layer beak`; import one at a time.
